title: Canada Deports Punjabi Youth in Surrey Extortion Crackdown
excerpt: Prabhjot Singh, 20, removed from Canada under Project Assurance as Surrey records 91 extortions and 16 shootings in 2026
body:
Surrey Police deported Prabhjot Singh, a 20-year-old Punjabi-origin foreign national, from Canada in early May 2026 after linking him to an active extortion racket in the city — the latest enforcement action under a sweeping crackdown on South Asian criminal networks.

**What happened:**
Surrey Police Service (SPS) arrested Singh earlier in 2026 on suspicion of extortion-related criminal activity and shared his details with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). The CBSA then conducted an independent immigration review that resulted in his removal from Canada. Singh was not alone: a second individual, Lovebir Singh (22), was deported under the same operation, and five others of Punjabi origin remain under active investigation.

**The bigger picture:**
Surrey recorded 91 reported extortions and 16 related shooting incidents since January 2026 alone. The removals fall under *Project Assurance*, an ongoing inter-agency operation targeting violent extortion networks linked to multiple shootings and intimidation campaigns across British Columbia. SPS Chief Constable Norm Lipinski said his force remains 'steadfastly committed to our policing colleagues and to our community in combatting the extortion crisis.' The crackdown sits inside a broader national surge: the CBSA removed 1,712 Indian citizens between January and March 2026 — nearly 32.5 per cent of all deportations in that period.

**What to watch:**
SPS released Singh's photograph publicly to identify associates still operating inside Canada, and the $250,000 Surrey Extortion Reward Fund — established in September 2025 — remains active for tips leading to convictions.

nri_angle: Indian-Americans with family ties to British Columbia's large Punjabi diaspora should take note: Canadian authorities are now using immigration enforcement as a direct tool against gang-linked foreign nationals, a policy shift that could reshape how South Asian communities across North America engage with law enforcement.
